rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient that spans the full practical organic range to reveal how many compounds elute in the gradient versus the final hold and to estimate the useful elution window. A midrange temperature gives a balanced first look at retention and selectivity without biasing too strongly toward very long or very short retention.

All 10 peaks are already fully resolved, so the only way to improve CRF is to pull the last peak earlier while preserving resolution. The estimated elution window is about phi≈0.09 to 0.41, so narrowing the gradient to a still-generous low-organic window and shortening tG should keep all peaks in-gradient and bring t_last closer to 10 min.

Changing the phi window made all peaks later, indicating the last peak is not being accelerated effectively by composition and may respond better to temperature. A hotter run should shorten retention across the board and may move t_last below 10 min while the current method has ample resolution margin.

At 60 C all pairs still have full-credit resolution, and the only remaining penalty is that the last peak is just past 10 min. A modestly steeper gradient should pull the last peak earlier while likely keeping the current worst pair above R=1.5, given the existing margin of 1.83.

The steeper 16 min gradient got t_last under 10 min but over-compressed the critical 4/5 pair, while 20 min had that pair safely resolved but t_last slightly too late. An intermediate tG of 18 min should restore the critical pair toward R>=1.5 while likely keeping the last peak at about 10 min or just under, which is the best route to CRF 1.0.

The only issue is the tight 4/5 pair versus the last peak slightly after 10 min; since that pair is temperature-sensitive, a small drop from 60 to 55 C should improve its selectivity while adding only a modest retention increase. With the 20 min gradient already giving full resolution at 60 C, this is the best chance to push the critical pair safely above 1.5 while keeping t_last near 10 min.

Keep the near-optimal 18 min, 60 C conditions but slightly lower phi1 to make the gradient a bit shallower in the region where the critical 4/5 pair elutes, aiming to lift that pair above R=1.5. Because the last peak elutes at only about phi_e≈0.50 in the successful runs, reducing phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 should have only a small effect on t_last.

At 18 min and 60 C the only miss is a marginal 4/5 pair, while lowering temperature clearly changes selectivity; trying 55 C at the same tG tests whether that specific pair improves enough to outweigh a modest increase in t_last. This is a targeted selectivity probe around the current best method rather than another broad change in gradient shape.

Lowering phi1 improved the critical 4/5 pair at 18 min but cost too much in t_last; combining that selectivity gain with a shorter tG should recover the time penalty. This directly targets the apparent sweet spot between injection 4 and 7, aiming for all pairs at full credit with t_last near or below 10 min.

With phi1 0.90 the critical 4/5 pair reached full-credit resolution at 18 min, so lengthening slightly should preserve that while moving the method toward the minimum time penalty boundary. This tests whether the best point is around phi1 0.90 and tG 20, where all pairs may remain resolved and t_last could land near 10 min.

At fixed 16 min, lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the 4/5 pair from 1.05 to 1.24 while keeping t_last under 10 min, so pushing one more step to phi1 0.85 may get that pair to full credit. The last peak should still remain near 10 min because its estimated elution composition is well below 0.85.

The 4/5 and 6/7 bottlenecks trade off with temperature, so a combined move to slightly lower phi1 and 55 C may rebalance selectivity better than either change alone. This tests whether the shallower window can rescue the pair that failed at 18 min, 55 C while keeping t_last close enough to 10 min.

Temperature is the only lever that has changed which pair is critical, so probing one more step lower tests whether a stronger selectivity shift can separate 4/5 enough to offset any new compression elsewhere. This is a deliberate boundary check around the current best settings before committing to local refinement.

The first peak is still fairly early, so a small increase in phi0 should compress the least retained region and may shift time budget toward the later part of the gradient, potentially shaving t_last with limited effect on the critical mid-eluting 4/5 pair. This tests whether start composition, which has not yet been explored, can improve the near-optimal 18 min, 60 C method.

Phi1 reductions improved the critical 4/5 pair at 18 min, and the last peak still elutes at a moderate effective composition, so one more step to phi1 0.80 tests whether that pair can be pushed comfortably above 1.5. This is a targeted check of whether added shallowness can compensate for the small time penalty better than the current best method.

A longer run at 60 C will map how much extra resolution the 4/5 pair gains per 2 min of gradient time beyond 20 min, giving a cleaner slope estimate for interpolation around the optimum than the mixed phi1 experiments. This helps determine whether the near-optimal 18 min result is fundamentally limited by the tG grid or whether another lever is still worth exploiting.

The data suggest the optimum may require compensating the 55 C selectivity shift with a shallower gradient window, and phi1 0.85 has not yet been tested at 18 min. This run checks whether 4/5 can stay resolved while the problematic 6/7 pair at lower temperature improves enough to beat the current near-tie best methods.

The trend with tG at 60 C shows a smooth tradeoff where 4/5 resolution decreases as the run is shortened; a 14 min run will define that slope more clearly and test whether the pair is highly nonlinear near the fast end. Even if not optimal itself, this gives the last needed anchor to judge whether the 18 min grid point is effectively the best attainable condition.

At 18 min, lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the critical 4/5 pair, so applying the same composition change to the 14 min fast method may recover substantial 4/5 resolution while keeping the attractive sub-10 min last peak. This is the best remaining chance to beat the current best by combining the fast timing of tG 14 with a shallower effective slope in the critical region.

The 4/5 pair improves steadily with longer tG at 60 C, and a 24 min point will show whether the gain is saturating or still linear enough that the true optimum is simply the shortest fully resolved method near 20 min. This final slope check helps confirm whether the current 0.986 result is effectively the grid-limited maximum.

At 14 min, lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the critical 4/5 pair while preserving the zero time penalty, so extending that trend to phi1 0.85 is the strongest remaining attempt to reach full-credit resolution in the fast regime. If 4/5 rises enough, this could outperform the current best because t_last is already safely below 10 min in the 14 min methods.

A higher phi0 strongly accelerated the run but hurt the 4/5 pair at 18 min; testing that idea at 20 min asks whether extra gradient time can recover the pair while keeping t_last around or below 10 min. This is one of the few unexplored combinations that could plausibly beat the current best by trading early compression for modestly restored selectivity.

The best runs suggest 4/5 resolution benefits from lower phi1 while 18 min and below are too fast, so 20 min with phi1 0.85 is a direct test of whether full-credit resolution can be achieved in that shallower window. If 4/5 remains resolved, this run will show whether the extra retention penalty is acceptable or confirms that the current best is the practical optimum.

A higher phi0 sharply reduced t_last but over-compressed the critical 4/5 pair, while lower phi1 tends to help that pair, so combining both at 20 min is a last structured attempt to balance those opposing effects. This unexplored corner could in principle keep the run under 10 min while restoring more 4/5 resolution than the high-phi0/high-phi1 test.

The last untested local combination around the fast/high-temperature region is phi1 0.80 at 16 min, which may further improve the 4/5 pair relative to 16 min with higher phi1 while still having a good chance to keep t_last near 10 min. This is a final targeted check for a better tradeoff than the current tied-best style methods before accepting injection 5 as the campaign winner.
